text: 🇲🇽🎨 16,289 young people — 5,761 from the US — entered Mexico's binational music contest for peace "Through this binational contest between Mexico and the United States for young people aged 18 to 29, we have brought together and united young people from Mexico and the United States, and strengthened bonds that clearly exist on both sides of the border. Music has no borders. More than 16,289 young people participated: 10,528 from Mexico, 5,761 from the United States." — Culture Secretary Claudia Curiel, morning press conference The Culture Ministry announced results of the second edition of "México Canta," a contest for original music without violent lyrics. The seven US semifinalists perform August 23 at Los Angeles' Million Dollar Theater; the final is September 13 at the Auditorio Nacional.

🇲🇽✊ El Bogueto at the National Palace: "You can achieve great things coming from the barrio" ""I want the message for those from the barrio, for people everywhere, to get motivated, to take the initiative to fulfill their dreams. It doesn't matter where you're from, it doesn't matter what people say or where you come from. If you don't have opportunities, here is clear proof that you can achieve great things coming from the barrio."" — El Bogueto, at the morning press conference Armando Toledo Rosas, "El Bogueto," an independent artist from Ciudad Nezahualcóyotl with over 24 million streams who never went through the music industry's circuits, joined the government's "México Canta" contest voluntarily as an ambassador. He performed his song "Mi Barrio" at the July 23, 2026 press conference alongside the seven Mexican-American semifinalists.

🇲🇽🎨 Sheinbaum on bans of narco-glorifying music: education, not prohibition — "if you prohibit it, people will keep listening anyway" ""On this we believe it is better to promote and raise awareness, not to prohibit. Because if you prohibit it, people will keep listening to it anyway. So it is really about education."" — President Sheinbaum, morning press conference Several Mexican states and municipalities have banned public performances of music that glorifies crime. Asked whether those bans fit her government's message, Sheinbaum said the federal approach is promotion and awareness rather than prohibition, while recognizing each state's right to legislate. She contrasted it with the junk food ban in schools, where the government did set limits to protect children's health.

🇲🇽✊ Sheinbaum: TV series turn drug capos into heroes — "that is not life for young people, that is death" "There were many television series — still on many platforms — that promote to young people the idea that if you get involved with a criminal group you will be successful, you will have money, women, a life of luxury. And then what happens to a young person? They turn a drug capo into a hero or a heroine. And we are against that, because that is not life for young people — that is death for young people." — President Sheinbaum, morning press conference Asked how "México Canta" counters the narco narrative in music, Sheinbaum criticized streaming series that glamorize drug trafficking. The alternative, she said, is education, scholarships and cultural promotion. The contest drew over 16,000 participants in its second edition.

🚨🇲🇽 Sheinbaum: 40 million Mexicans in the US work honestly and contribute to the US economy — that bond never breaks "There are almost 40 million Mexicans living in the United States who work honestly, who support their families, who help Mexico, who contribute to the US economy. And there is a cultural bond that never breaks: the origin, the values, the identity still felt in Mexican families of the first, second, third, even fourth generation in the United States." — President Sheinbaum, morning press conference Presenting the seven Mexican-American semifinalists of the "México Canta" contest, Sheinbaum framed it as a defense of the cultural bond with the diaspora, against a bilateral narrative dominated by drugs and weapons. The contest drew 5,761 participants from the US this year.

🇲🇽🌎 Sheinbaum debunks US senators' claim that Mexico is failing its water treaty obligations: "That is false" ""They told him that we are not complying with the water quota. And that is false — we are complying perfectly and there is full agreement with the United States. And this year, when we expect even more rain, it will be fulfilled. There is no problem whatsoever with the water issue at this moment."" — President Sheinbaum, morning press conference On July 22, 2026, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer appeared before the US Senate, where Texas senators claimed Mexico was not delivering its water quota under the 1944 Water Treaty. Sheinbaum rejected the claim the next morning, stating Mexico is in full compliance, that there is total agreement with the US government, and that this year's deliveries will be met.

🚨🇲🇽 "The US unilaterally decided to impose tariffs on the entire world" — Sheinbaum ahead of meeting with US Trade Representative Greer ""You know that the United States unilaterally decided to impose tariffs on the entire world. Now comes this round of tariffs under Section 301. We don't know exactly where Mexico will stand. What I can tell you is that we have done everything humanly possible so that Mexico gets the best possible conditions, always defending the interests of the country."" — President Sheinbaum, morning press conference Hours before receiving US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer at the National Palace on July 23, 2026, Sheinbaum addressed the new round of Section 301 tariffs announced by Washington. The talks cover trade only; security is handled in separate coordination tables.

🇲🇽📉 <u>MEXICO'S INFLATION FALLS TO 3.10% — LOWEST SINCE DECEMBER 2020</u>

Mexico's inflation fell to 3.10% annual in the first half of July, its lowest since the second half of December 2020, INEGI reported — deep inside Banxico's 2-4% target range and down from 4.53% in early April.

The consumer price index rose just 0.07% in the fortnight. Non-core inflation is up barely 0.21% over the year: fruits and vegetables fell 1.50%, led by tomatoes at -13.18%. The minimum consumption basket did not move at all.

Via El Financiero.

🇲🇽🎶 <u>"MÉXICO CANTA": SHEINBAUM PRESENTS 7 MEXICAN-AMERICAN SEMIFINALISTS SINGING FOR PEACE</u>

President Sheinbaum presented the seven Mexican-American semifinalists of México Canta 2026, the binational contest where young people sing for peace and against addictions on both sides of the border.

"We talk little about the bond of love, of culture, of everyday life of the families who live on one side and the other of the border — and that bond never breaks," she said. "They are Americans, but they keep feeling Mexican. And that is something truly beautiful."

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>SENATE RECEIVES SHEINBAUM'S FEMINICIDE LAW: UP TO 70 YEARS IN PRISON</u>

Mexico's Senate officially received the presidential initiative for a General Law to Prevent, Investigate, Punish and Repair the Crime of Feminicide — the first nationwide legal framework against the most extreme form of violence against women.

The proposal contemplates sentences of up to 70 years in prison and creates a National Registry of Children and Adolescents Orphaned by Feminicide, to guarantee protection and reparations for indirect victims. Senate president Laura Itzel Castillo said it goes straight to the Justice and Gender Equality commissions — the goal: unified investigation criteria across the country, and an end to impunity.
